title: Tensoring a trace transpose and the exceptional tensor arrow
statement:
Use the finite coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale derived categories and the derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the compact-support functors [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and their constructible exceptional adjoints [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $\otimes$ for $\otimes_A^L$.

Let $f:V\to S$ be separated finite type, put $\omega_f=Rf^!A_S$, let $L\in D^b_c(V,A)$, and let $t:Rf_!L\to A_S$ have transpose $P:L\to\omega_f$. Fix $K\in D^b_{ctf}(S,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Assume the canonical compact-support projection maps [def-exchange-projection] at $(L,K)$ and $(\omega_f,K)$ are invertible. Let
$$\Pi_{M,K}:Rf_!(Lf^*K\otimes M)\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes Rf_!M$$
be the inverse projection map with the two tensor symmetries inserted. Define $\theta_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes\omega_f\to Rf^!K$ to be the transpose of $(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_{f,A_S})\circ\Pi_{\omega_f,K}$, followed by the tensor-unit constraint, as in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Then
$$\theta_{f,K}\circ(1\otimes P)
=\operatorname{adj}_f\bigl((1_K\otimes t)\circ\Pi_{L,K}\bigr),$$
where $\operatorname{adj}_f$ is the exceptional Hom bijection and both tensor-unit constraints are understood. The equality is natural in $K$ on the stated domain and does not require $f$ smooth, $P$ invertible or an orientation of $\omega_f$.

proof.text:
By the definition of the exceptional transpose, the map $P:L\to\omega_f$ is characterized by the counit equation
$$\varepsilon_{f,A_S}\circ Rf_!(P)=t,$$
with the coefficient-unit identifications understood. This is the only property of $P$ used below.

source.place: Displayed exceptional Hom bijection and the following paragraph on bounded-below etale-origin inputs; elementary counit equation

proof.text:
Put $X_K=Lf^*K\otimes\omega_f$ and $u=1\otimes P$. Define $e_K:Rf_!X_K	o K$ by
$$e_K=\lambda_K\circ(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_{f,A_S})\circ\Pi_{\omega_f,K},$$
where $\lambda_K:K\otimes A_S\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ is the unit constraint. The two symmetries are already included in $\Pi$; no additional symmetry precedes it. By the definition of $\theta_{f,K}$, $\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(\theta_{f,K})=e_K$. Therefore functoriality gives
$$\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(\theta_{f,K}\circ u)=e_K\circ Rf_!(u).$$
This is the inverse exceptional transpose of the composite in the assertion.

source.place: Condition 2: canonical map is the mate of the projection formula with the adjunction counit; explicit counit calculation written here

proof.text:
The projection transformation is natural in its first coefficient, so invertibility of the two displayed projection maps gives naturality of their inverses. Therefore, after the canonical associators and symmetries,
$$\Pi_{\omega_f,K}\circ Rf_!(1\otimes P)=(1_K\otimes Rf_!P)\circ\Pi_{L,K}.$$
Substituting this into the preceding transpose and using the counit equation from Step 1 yields
$$e_K\circ Rf_!(1\otimes P)=(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_{f,A_S})\circ(1_K\otimes Rf_!P)\circ\Pi_{L,K}=(1_K\otimes t)\circ\Pi_{L,K}.$$
The last equality is functoriality of derived tensor and the tensor-unit constraint.

source.place: Final projection-transformation paragraphs: definition and naturality in both coefficients; invert the naturality square on the assumed isomorphism domain

proof.text: Both maps in the claimed equality have now been shown to have the same exceptional adjunction transpose, namely $(1_K\otimes t)\circ\Pi_{L,K}$. The exceptional Hom bijection is injective, so the maps themselves are equal. Naturality in $K$ follows because every map used above—$\Pi$, tensor symmetry, the counit, and the adjunction bijection—is natural in $K$ on the stated domain.
